$comment: Region -> governing-doc register (tempdoc 620 Move 2). CONSULT IT WHEN YOU EDIT A PATH IT COVERS: the row names the docs to read and, where present, the recipe to run. Tempdoc 930 row 4 retired the two hooks that used to push rows automatically (a PreToolUse consult hint and a Stop maintain block), so this register is now read, not delivered. Machine consumer: scripts/ci/run-ui-web-gates.mjs parses the `ui-web-gates` row's recipe as the single authority for the ui-web gate set (its command count is floor-checked, so the recipe prose must keep parsing). Schema per row: pathIncludes (array of path substrings; matches if the edited path contains any) + region (label) + docs ([{path, why}] to read before editing) + maintain (optional bool; when true, the row's docs are expected to be updated in the same PR as a change to the region) + recipe (optional array of step strings -- a numbered just-in-time procedure, the relocation home for path-triggerable workflow recipes evicted from the always-loaded layer, e.g. common-workflows.md's gRPC/REST/config/agent-tool recipes, tempdoc 620 Phase 2; a recipe row typically sets docs:[]). A delivery row is how the always-loaded layer evicts region-specific context: read it only when the region is touched.

docs.why: the frontend is **Lit web components**, not React (the React stack is retired).
single presentation authorities (tone/originator/layout/modality); a re-authored badge/modal/transient is meant to be unrepresentable, not just discouraged.

recipe: Editing CoreSurfaceCatalog.java — run node scripts/ci/check-surface-composition.mjs. Tempdoc 852 S0 gave that gate a parity leg: a surface id declared in BOTH this file and modules/ui-web/src/shell-v0/plugin-api/CorePlugin.ts must agree on audience and placement. No other gate can see a one-sided change — the interaction-surface gate parses this file only, check-window-cutover reads CorePlugin.ts only — so moving one side alone ships a broken or duplicated USER window with every gate green. The ui-web-gates recipe already covers the CorePlugin.ts direction; this row covers the Java one.

Also run node scripts/governance/run.mjs --gate surface-altitude --mode gate (a surface's altitude is DERIVED from the authorities it consumes, so a new or changed Surface(...) can create a derivation conflict).

Any modules/ui-web/src/** edit — run the ui-web gate set before merge (node scripts/ci/<name>.mjs): check-adaptive-closure, check-layout-purity, check-surface-composition, check-message-single-model, check-run-renderers, check-inflight-liveness, check-composition-surfaces, check-declared-surfaces, check-live-channels, check-contrast-matrix, check-style-literal-ratchet.

Tempdoc 930 row 9 (chunk H) retired the recipe's 12 static a11y/contrast/token oracles (full list: tempdoc 930 section 19.3 finding F10) in favor of measured axe (ui-shot + governance/ui-a11y-baseline.v1.json) and review, since every traced a11y/contrast catch came from one of those, never from a static oracle. check-contrast-matrix (the four-palette sweep) and every register-backed check stay in the recipe above. gen-token-names and gen-component-vocabulary remain as codegen scripts (their generated files are still compiled against) — only their --check gate registration was removed.

Plus the kernel gates: node scripts/governance/run.mjs --gate ambient-purity --gate atom-fork-ratchet --gate modality-contract --gate transient-arbitration --gate modal-arbitration --mode gate (`--gate` is repeatable; it does NOT split on commas — tempdoc 932; `node scripts/ci/run-ui-web-gates.mjs` expands this list and runs the whole set, tempdoc 872).

modules/ui-web/src/shell-v0/** edits additionally: check-steering-arbitration, check-search-issuance, check-verdict-derivation, check-ai-verdict-derivation, check-message-classes, check-capability-availability, check-realized-capability, check-consequence-classification, check-folder-status-derivation.
shell-v0/views/** edits additionally: check-surface-task-state-retention, check-thread-event-kinds.

Frontend lint + typecheck + unit tests: cd modules/ui-web && npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm run test:unit:run. (Relocated from the CLAUDE.md Pre-merge table — tempdoc 681; check-premerge-table validates these refs here.) `npm run lint` is `eslint . --max-warnings=0` — tempdoc 930 §22.2 follow-up 8 made warnings and unused `eslint-disable` directives fail, so the ts-any/todo-fixme successors cannot rot back into advisories. It is NOT parsed into this runner's command list: it needs `npm ci --prefix modules/ui-web`, and this runner deliberately runs in CI ABOVE that install. CI runs it as the separate "Frontend lint" step.

regions.region: the UI measurement baselines (a11y known-rules / chrome proportion)
recipe: Editing governance/ui-a11y-baseline.v1.json or governance/ui-proportion-baseline.v1.json (or either .schema.json) — run node scripts/ci/check-ui-baseline-schemas.mjs. Both registers declare a relative $schema, and until that gate landed nothing read those pointers: ui-a11y-baseline named ./ui-a11y-baseline.schema.json from the day it shipped and the file did not exist, so the register was unvalidated while LOOKING validated. The gate asserts the pointer resolves, the schema compiles, and the document conforms — plus that no two a11y rows share a uiShotStep, which draft-07 cannot express and which would give one capture two accepted rule sets.
A schema edit is an authority edit: if you add a field to a register, add it to its schema in the same change, or the gate fails on the additionalProperties: false it deliberately keeps.

regions.region: the loopback egress / inbound-access security surface

docs.why: the privacy guarantee ('nothing leaves your machine') and its mechanical anchors (CSP loopback-lock, Host/Origin/token filters, no telemetry) — re-verify the threat model if you change the CSP or the request-filter security plumbing.
the agent loop, operation-substrate tool dispatch, token budget, durability, and the MCP tool surface -- read before changing agent behavior (616 read-0x delivery).
HNSW search, SPLADE learned-sparse retrieval, hybrid fusion, and the commit-metadata system -- the ranking-quality surface (616 read-0x delivery).
how the Worker builds ORT sessions and wires the six encoder roles onto one typed composition pipeline (616 read-0x delivery).

recipe: Define the method + messages in the .proto (e.g. indexing.proto).
Implement the service method in modules/worker-services/.
Add the forward in DelegatingIngestService.java (modules/indexer-worker/.../grpc/) — the server registers this wrapper, not the impl; without it the RPC returns UNIMPLEMENTED at runtime.
Add the client call in modules/app-services/ (RemoteKnowledgeClient or the relevant client).
Add a contract test.
Verify: ./gradlew.bat :modules:ipc-common:build :modules:worker-services:test :modules:indexer-worker:test
Full reference: docs/reference/contributing/common-workflows.md (Add a gRPC method).
Add the handler/controller under modules/ui/src/main/java/.../api/.
Register the route via the relevant .../api/routes/*Routes.java class, then wire that route class from LocalApiServer.java if needed.
Update docs/reference/api-contract-map.md if the endpoint is public.
Honor the Hard Invariants: loopback-only bind (127.0.0.1), no legacy endpoints (/api/search, /api/settings), and Head never touches Lucene — delegate index IO to the Worker via gRPC.
Verify: ./gradlew.bat :modules:ui:test
Full reference: docs/reference/contributing/common-workflows.md (Add a REST endpoint).
Add the entry in EnvRegistry.java (operator-facing) or ConfigKey.java (YAML-only).
Wire it in ResolvedConfigBuilder.java — add a putYaml*() contribution + a resolve*() call in the relevant build*().
Expose it via a ResolvedConfig record field.
Document it in docs/reference/configuration/environment-variables.md.
Verify: ./gradlew.bat :modules:configuration:test

Regrowth ratchet (tempdoc 799 K.4): a NET-NEW key fails the config-surface gate. Run `node scripts/docs/generate-runtime-config-matrix.mjs` then `node scripts/governance/run.mjs --gate config-surface --mode gate`. Growth is allowed but must be DECLARED — add a changeset under gates/config-surface/.changesets/ classified `declared-growth` with a tempdoc/adr justification. Before declaring, check the knob is not already shadowed by a hardcoded constant: tempdoc 754 found 28 that were (a documented knob that does nothing is worse than no knob).
Full reference: docs/reference/contributing/common-workflows.md (Add a configuration key).

docs.why: this ADR is why JustSearch treats operation metadata as ENFORCED policy rather than MCP-style untrusted hints. The divergence is justified BY the enforcement, so an axis that stops being enforced invalidates the argument, not just the prose.

recipe: Add/update the operation definition in CoreOperationCatalog (modules/app-services/.../registry/operations/) or AgentToolsOperationCatalog (modules/app-agent/src/main/java/io/justsearch/agent/tools/AgentToolsOperationCatalog.java).

Implement/update the handler. The five knowledge/file agent tools ARE their own OperationHandlers — SearchTool, BrowseTool, IngestTool, ReadDocumentTool and FileOperationsTool in modules/app-agent/src/main/java/io/justsearch/agent/tools/ implement the interface directly, with no adapter class in between. Two agent operations, core.remember and core.navigate-to-surface, keep dedicated handlers in modules/app-services/.../registry/operations/handlers/, as do all non-agent operations.
Confirm AgentToolEmitter projects the intended model-visible wire name + schema.

Declare safety/approval metadata at the operation layer, and run node scripts/ci/check-policy-axis-liveness.mjs. Tempdoc 879: every OperationPolicy axis must have a production reader outside the registry validators, and every Optional axis must be declared by at least one operation. An axis that fails is not 'not wired yet' — wire it to a consumer whose behaviour the declaration changes, or delete it (field, every declaration site, validators, wire projection, both schema copies, generated FE types, docs). There is deliberately no opt-out: an escape hatch for 'declared ahead of its consumer' is the deferral this gate exists to refuse.
Update docs/explanation/22-agent-system-architecture.md.
Verify: ./gradlew.bat :modules:app-agent:test :modules:app-services:test
Full reference: docs/reference/contributing/common-workflows.md (Add an agent tool).

regions.region: the models/ tree (weights are never tracked in this repo)
recipe: This public repo NEVER tracks model blobs — 0 .onnx in its history; CI builds without them.
models/.gitignore excludes the weights so `git add -A` cannot stage ~2.6 GB via the *.onnx LFS filter. Do not 'fix' that ignore rule.

The PRIVATE repo LFS-tracks them, so the inherited rule 'do not gitignore model files' applies THERE and was carried here at v0.1.0 despite never being true of this repo (inherited-authority drift — tempdoc 799 §C.4).

regions.region: the index field schema / document extraction path
recipe: Adding a field to fields.v1.json or changing extraction in IndexingDocumentOps does NOT update existing documents.
Existing indices must be REBUILT: `jseval run --reset` (eval mode) or `jseval run --start-backend --clean`.
Test corpora indexed before your change will silently lack the new fields — a green run over a stale corpus proves nothing about the new field.

regions.region: the justsearch-dev MCP surface (the agent-facing dev tools)

docs.why: the canonical inventory of this surface — tool list, fetch_api_json endpoint keys, api_call allowlist. Tempdoc 844 §6.3 found the same inventory stated in four places and wrong in all four, because nothing compared the doc to the server. Update this page in the SAME change as the tool registration.

recipe: Adding, removing or renaming a tool / an endpoint key / an allowlist entry: update docs/reference/contributing/mcp-dev-tools.md in the same change (the tool table AND the `exposes exactly these **N** tools` count).
Then run `node scripts/ci/check-dev-mcp-doc-sync.mjs` — it spawns the server, calls tools/list, and compares all three inventories in both directions. It needs no dev stack.

Changing the SDK/Zod runtime boundary or root MCP dependencies: run `node scripts/dev/generate-dev-mcp-runtime.mjs`, then `node scripts/dev/generate-dev-mcp-runtime.mjs --check` and `node scripts/dev/generate-dev-mcp-runtime.test.mjs`. Commit both generated outputs, including the legal projection.

Changing bootstrap/import behavior: run `node scripts/dev/test-dev-mcp-bootstrap.mjs`; it proves the exact committed launcher in a dependency-free Git fixture and checks stable negative diagnostics with no stdout.
Changing file/socket observation behavior or quick_health/preflight truth states: run `node scripts/dev/test-dev-mcp-observations.mjs` in addition to the handler-level suites.
If you changed the gate itself, run its co-located test too: `node scripts/ci/check-dev-mcp-doc-sync.test.mjs`.

Changing tool BEHAVIOUR (projection, probes, error codes, dist resolution): run `node scripts/dev/test-dev-mcp-surface-honesty.mjs` (pure units) and `node scripts/dev/test-dev-mcp-projection-live.mjs` (real handlers over stdio against a throwaway loopback backend). Neither needs a dev stack.

Tempdoc 844 §12.2 is the standing criterion for this surface: a dev tool must not report state it did not verify, and must not report success it did not confirm — an explicit unknown (`null`) beats a confident default (`[]`, `false`, `OK`).

regions.region: an architecture decision record (ADR) or the architectural risk register

docs.why: the ADR conventions and the § How to re-examine an ADR procedure — an ADR is amended append-only, and every edit owes a refreshed `last_reviewed:` plus a `probes:` entry that still restates the decision's premise. Editing an ADR's prose without those is the drift the probe register exists to catch.

recipe: Changing a decision (not a typo): follow docs/decisions/README.md § How to re-examine an ADR. Amendments are APPEND-ONLY — add a dated amendment section, do not rewrite the original Decision/Context in place; the superseded reasoning is the record.

Set `last_reviewed: YYYY-MM-DD` to today in the frontmatter. That date is the cadence: the adr-coverage gate warns past the window declared as `reviewStaleDays` in governance/adr-probes.v1.json (183 days), and node scripts/agent-analytics/world-state.mjs lists the same ADRs in its ADR review section (the manual orientation command AGENTS.md points you at, not an automatic session-start hook).

Check the ADR's `probes:` still restates the NEW premise. A probe that passes against the old decision is worse than no probe — it reports green about a claim the ADR no longer makes. Update or replace the entry in governance/adr-probes.v1.json; never edit a probe merely to make it pass.
A live (accepted*/stable*) ADR must name a probe or state a reason: `probes: none - <reason>`. A bare `probes: none` states nothing and still fails.
Verify: node scripts/governance/run.mjs --gate adr-coverage --mode gate.
If the decision changed inside a tempdoc, the ADR update rides in the SAME PR — see docs/reference/contributing/agent-guide.md §3.8.

regions.region: Java on the head-process classpath (dev-stack freshness)
recipe: The MCP justsearch_dev_start does not always re-install the worker dist when upstream Gradle tasks report UP-TO-DATE.

After editing Java here (or in any module on the head-process classpath), run `./gradlew.bat :modules:ui:installDist` explicitly BEFORE dev_start / restart, so the jar in modules/ui/build/install/ui/lib/ is fresh.
Symptom if skipped: the wire payload reflects the PREVIOUS build despite a successful `gradlew build`. Discovered tempdoc 511-followup Track E live-verify.
